title: No sound and "No audio output device is installed" (red X on speaker icon)
symptoms: Speaker icon in the taskbar shows a red X
Hovering the speaker icon says "No audio output device is installed"
Settings > System > Sound says "No output devices found"
causes: The playback device was disabled in Sound settings or Device Manager
The audio driver is missing, corrupted, or not loading
A driver installed by Windows Update broke the audio device
The Windows Audio or Windows Audio Endpoint Builder service is stopped

signals: No active render (playback) audio endpoint exists
A playback endpoint exists but is in the Disabled state
A device under Sound, video and game controllers (MEDIA class) is disabled (problem code 22) or has an error such as code 10
The Audiosrv or AudioEndpointBuilder service is not running

fixes.title: Run the Windows audio troubleshooter
steps: On Windows 11, open the Get Help app and run the Audio troubleshooter, or go to Settings > System > Sound and select Troubleshoot under the output device.
On Windows 10, go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Playing Audio and select Run the troubleshooter.
Apply any fixes it suggests, then test the sound.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, Windows 10 and 11
Official Dell KB, step 8

fixes.title: Re-enable a disabled playback device
steps: Press Win + R, type mmsys.cpl, and press Enter.
On the Playback tab, right-click an empty area and select Show Disabled Devices.
Right-click your speakers or headphones, select Enable, then select Set as Default Device and OK.
If the device is not listed, open Device Manager, expand Sound, video and game controllers, right-click the audio device and select Enable device if that option is shown.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page, Solution 1: Enable device in Device Manager
Microsoft Community Support Specialist answer, 100+ helpful votes; question asked 800+ times

fixes.title: Restart the Windows audio services
steps: Press Win + R, type services.msc, and press Enter.
Right-click Windows Audio Endpoint Builder and select Restart.
Right-click Windows Audio and select Restart, or Start if it is stopped.
Make sure both services have Startup type set to Automatic.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: restart Windows Audio, Windows Audio Endpoint Builder and RPC
Microsoft Tech Community thread, reply marked as solution (step 2: services running and Automatic)

fixes.title: Uninstall the audio device and let Windows reinstall it
steps: Right-click Start and open Device Manager.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click your audio device and select Uninstall device.
Select Attempt to remove the driver for this device (Windows 11) or Delete the driver software for this device (Windows 10), then select Uninstall.
Restart the PC so Windows reinstalls the device. If it does not reappear, open Device Manager and select Action > Scan for hardware changes.
If Windows does not install a working driver, install the latest audio driver from your PC or motherboard maker's support site.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page, uninstall driver step
Official Intel support article for "no audio output device is installed" after Windows update
Official Dell KB, step 4

fixes.title: Switch to the Windows built-in High Definition Audio Device driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click the audio device and select Update driver.
Select Browse my computer for drivers, then Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer.
Select High Definition Audio Device and select Next. Confirm the warning if shown.
Restart the PC and test the sound. Note that maker-specific features such as audio tuning apps may stop working with this driver.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: use the Windows-supplied generic audio driver / select High Definition Audio Device
Official Intel article: Update driver > Let me pick from a list > choose audio driver
User reply: "I tried loading the generic Microsoft driver and problem solved" (0 likes)

fixes.title: Roll back the audio driver after a Windows Update
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers.
Right-click the audio device and select Properties.
On the Driver tab, select Roll Back Driver and follow the prompts.
Restart the PC. If Roll Back Driver is greyed out, use System Restore to a restore point from before the update.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: roll back driver if audio broke after Windows Update
User reply (Lenovo IdeaPad 3): rolling back the Realtek driver fixed it

title: No sound because the Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio controller fails with Code 10
symptoms: No sound after a Windows, driver, or BIOS update
"No audio output device is installed" on a laptop with Intel audio
Device Manager shows a yellow warning on Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) Audio Controller or Intel SST OED with Code 10
causes: The Intel SST audio controller driver failed to start after an update
The installed Intel SST driver does not match the laptop's audio codec driver

signals: A System devices entry named Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller or Intel SST OED has ConfigManagerErrorCode 10
No active playback audio endpoint exists

fixes.title: Switch the Intel SST Audio Controller to the High Definition Audio Controller driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand System devices.
Right-click Intel(R) Smart Sound Technology (Intel(R) SST) Audio Controller and select Update driver.
Select Browse my computer for drivers, then Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer.
Select High Definition Audio Controller and select Next.
Select Action > Scan for hardware changes, or restart the PC, and test the sound.

sources.signal: Official Intel support article for SST Code 10 with no audio
Dell Community thread marked Solved; original poster: "This solved the issue on both devices"; another user: "this solves the issue"

fixes.title: Install the audio driver from the PC maker
steps: Open the support site of your PC maker (for example Dell, HP or Lenovo) and enter your model or service tag.
Download the latest audio driver (often Realtek) and, if listed, the Intel SST or chipset driver for your Windows version.
Install the drivers and restart the PC.

sources.signal: Official Intel article: get the audio driver from the computer manufacturer; OEM versions may include changes
Community Accepted Solution (Dell Realtek driver); users confirm: "Now my audio working normal", "fixed the large majority of them"

title: Speaker icon looks normal and volume meters move, but nothing is heard
symptoms: The speaker icon has no red X
The Volume mixer or Sound control panel shows the level meter moving
No sound comes out of the speakers or headphones
causes: Sound is going to a different output, such as a monitor without speakers over HDMI or DisplayPort
The device, the app, or the physical speakers are muted or turned down
Audio enhancements from the driver are silencing or breaking the output

signals: The default playback endpoint is not the device the user expects (for example an HDMI/DisplayPort display endpoint)
The default endpoint or an app session is muted or at 0% volume
Audio enhancements are turned on for the default playback device

fixes.title: Choose the right output device and check mute and app volume
steps: Select the speaker icon in the taskbar and confirm your speakers or headphones are selected as the output.
Open Settings > System > Sound and pick the correct output device. Monitors without built-in speakers can appear as an output device.
Make sure the device is not muted and the volume is turned up, including the physical volume on the speakers.
Open the Volume mixer and make sure the app you are using is not muted and its slider is up.
Check that cables are in the correct jack and that the speakers are powered on. Unplug headphones in case they are taking the sound.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: check output device, hardware and volume, set default device (USB/HDMI/monitors without speakers)
Official Dell KB, step 6: confirm correct output device, review App volume and device preferences

fixes.title: Turn off audio enhancements for the output device
steps: On Windows 11, open Settings > System > Sound, select your output device, and set Audio enhancements to Off.

On Windows 10, open Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Sound, select the default playback device, select Properties, and on the Enhancements tab check Disable all enhancements (or Disable all sound effects).
Test the sound. If it does not help, turn enhancements back on.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page, step: Turn off audio enhancements
